description: Adversarial conformance fixtures for SCITT-style envelope verification, built against Cedulon/emiliaprotocol thread (scitt@ietf.org, Nicholas/Dogru). Both vectors are 'self-consistent' claims that a lenient verifier can pass by checking only internal consistency, without checking against an independent ground truth (a trust root registry, or the actual preimage bytes). Both MUST fail closed with a named failure_mode field distinct from the other's boundary, not a shared boolean.
related_bugs_shape: Vernon boolean collapse — signature-valid treated as authenticity-proven
Joel ABSENT collapse — three distinct 'no linkage' states folded into one value
Emek tailPinned — pinned/anchored state not independently distinguished from claimed state

trust_registry.note: Simulates an independent, out-of-band trust anchor registry. A verifier MUST check membership here, not just that a signature verifies against SOME embedded key.

vectors.description: Card is internally self-consistent: the signature verifies correctly against the embedded issuer public key, and that key was freshly generated for this card (key_created_at == card_issued_at, key_source='embedded_self_generated'). Nothing about the card's internal structure is malformed. But the embedded key does not chain to any entry in the independent trust anchor registry — the card proves only that its own claimed issuer signed it, not that the issuer is a party anyone should trust.
vectors.failure_detail: card.issuer_key_id='self-forged-9f21a' has a cryptographically valid Ed25519 signature over its own claim (self_consistency=true, verified against the embedded issuer_pubkey), but is absent from trust_registry.known_trust_anchors. authenticity=false. A verifier that stops at signature verification (self-consistency) without a second, independent check against the trust root MUST NOT be considered conformant.

vectors.description: Control vector — same shape as above, but issuer_key_id resolves to a key chained under a registry-known trust anchor. Must PASS to prove the check isn't rejecting everything.

The envelope's preimage field, instead of containing the actual preimage object that SHA-256(JCS(preimage)) reduces to canonical_envelope_ref, contains the literal text of the canonicalization rule ('JCS RFC 8785 over {agent_id,action_type,scope,timestamp}') as a string. A verifier that does not attempt real recomputation — e.g. one that just checks 'preimage field is non-empty' — silently accepts this. A conformant verifier MUST attempt SHA-256(JCS(preimage)) and, on type/shape mismatch (preimage is not the expected object), reject named-boundary — not coerce to a boolean pass/fail without saying which boundary broke.
vectors.failure_detail: envelope.preimage is a str, not the 4-field preimage object {agent_id,action_type,scope,timestamp} required by action-ref.md#Derivation. SHA-256(JCS(preimage)) cannot be computed against the declared shape. This is a named-boundary rejection distinct from TRUST_ANCHOR_UNRESOLVED above — the two MUST NOT share a failure code or collapse into one boolean 'invalid':true.

vectors.description: Control vector — preimage is the real object, recomputes byte-identical to canonical_envelope_ref. Must PASS.

Card claims a trust-anchor-chained issuer_key_id and a registry-known trust_anchor_ref, and even asserts self_consistency=true in the artifact itself, but card_issued_at was mutated after signing -- the signature no longer verifies against the current card bytes. Proves the verifier computes self-consistency instead of trusting the artifact's own claim about itself (the exact gap in the pre-erratum verifier).
vectors.failure_detail: card.self_consistency=true is asserted by the artifact, but re-signing bytes (excluding signature/self_consistency fields) and verifying against issuer_pubkey fails -- card_issued_at was changed after the signature was produced. A verifier that reads the self_consistency field instead of computing it would wrongly accept this.
